clips.start_words: A past member of the FDA
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau cites a claim from a former FDA commissioner: drugs, taken exactly as directed, cause more deaths a year than the conditions they're prescribed for.

His example: Tylenol. A headache or a sore back won't end a life on its own, but Kevin's source ties the drug itself to around 2,000 deaths a year, used exactly as the label says.

His bigger point: many conditions people medicate daily, like psoriasis, were never life-threatening to begin with.

Comment HEALTH for what to ask before you take anything daily.
